subject: washing raw chicken in a sink
title: What If You Always Washed Raw Chicken?

scenes.text: What if you always rinsed raw chicken before cooking? You'd be cleaning it onto everything else.
Tap water splashes off the meat. Studies suggest droplets can travel up to about three feet.
In a USDA kitchen study, sixty percent of people who washed chicken left bacteria in the sink.
Fourteen percent still had bacteria in the sink even after they tried to clean it.
And twenty-six percent got chicken bacteria onto the salad they made next.
The twist? Even washing didn't make it cleaner. Only cooking to seventy-four degrees Celsius kills the bacteria.

description:
What if you always washed raw chicken? In a USDA study, 60% of people who washed poultry had bacteria in the sink afterwards, 14% still did after cleaning it, and 26% transferred bacteria to their salad.
Splashing can spread germs up to about 3 feet; food agencies advise not washing raw chicken and cooking it to 74 degrees Celsius (165 F).
